items.title: (Weak) solutions descend along the intermediate extension of discrete valuation rings and compose
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement concerns a tower of three extensions of discrete valuation rings and a finite extension of the bottom fraction field, and says that being a (weak) solution descends to the intermediate extension and composes from the intermediate extension to the top when the reduced base change is a product of fields that are themselves (weak) solutions (statement lines 34516-34527). The proof takes the reduced base changes and the corresponding integral closures, observes through the construction remark that the map between the closures is a finite product of the standard maps and hence surjective on spectra, chooses a maximal ideal and reduces to a chain of three discrete valuation rings, where weak unramifiedness and separability of residue extensions visibly pass to the intermediate extension (proof lines 34529-34552). The reduction to a single chain of localizations is the device that makes both assertions follow from elementary properties of the composite. The counted span refers twice to results of this chapter, both carried as navigation stubs.
